process_map.name: Workforce Planning & Shift Management
activities: Forecast baggage volumes and staffing needs
Allocate staff to shifts and implement rest breaks and task rotation policies
Adjust resourcing (e.g., hire additional staff) to prevent overwork
process_map.objective: Ensure staffing levels and work schedules prevent excessive physical strain and meet safety requirements
process_map.source_quote: Baggage handlers can reduce physical strain by ensuring varied tasks or hiring more staff.

process_map.name: Baggage Loading & Unloading Operations
activities: Retrieve and sort baggage in the airport baggage halls
Load and unload luggage into aircraft cargo holds on the tarmac
Transfer baggage carts between terminal facilities and aircraft
process_map.objective: Handle passenger baggage efficiently while minimizing manual lifting risks and ensuring worker safety
process_map.source_quote: Issues have been noted during the loading and unloading of passenger baggage in airport basements and at aircraft on the aprons.

process_map.name: Use of Mechanical Aids & Equipment
activities: Deploy lifting aids (hoists, conveyors, etc.) at baggage handling stations
Train employees in proper usage of mechanical aids for heavy items
Monitor and encourage consistent use of mechanised tools to reduce manual lifting
process_map.objective: Minimise manual lifting by leveraging mechanical assistance, thereby reducing workers' physical strain and injury risk
process_map.source_quote: The Labour Inspectorate was not satisfied with how lifting aids were being used by baggage handlers.

process_map.name: Health & Safety Training and Awareness
activities: Conduct regular training on safe lifting techniques and ergonomics
Provide safety briefings and refreshers highlighting proper use of aids and task rotation
Communicate regulatory requirements and company safety procedures to all employees
process_map.objective: Ensure all employees are aware of safe work practices and the importance of using aids and varying tasks to prevent injuries
process_map.source_quote: New measures were imposed to increase awareness and urgency among handlers in tackling excessive workload.

process_map.name: Incident Reporting & Investigation
activities: Report any work-related injuries or overexertion incidents through the internal system
Investigate each incident to identify root causes (e.g., workload issues, equipment failure)
Implement corrective actions and share lessons learned to prevent recurrence
process_map.objective: Identify and address any cases of worker overexertion or injury promptly, to improve conditions and ensure compliance with safety obligations
process_map.source_quote: Progress has been made, but the healthy working environment still does not meet the required standards.

process_map.name: Performance Monitoring & H&S Metrics
activities: Track key H&S metrics (injury rates, average weight lifted per shift, aid utilisation rate)
Conduct regular ergonomic risk assessments and workplace observations
Review compliance data (task rotation, break adherence) and report trends to management
process_map.objective: Continuously monitor physical workload and safety performance, allowing for timely interventions and demonstration of compliance improvements
process_map.source_quote: The Labour Inspectorate warned that further fines may follow if working conditions do not improve sufficiently.

process_map.name: Regulatory Compliance & Enforcement Response
activities: Keep abreast of labour safety regulations and Inspectorate requirements
Coordinate responses to any Inspectorate notices or fines (prepare objections, remediate issues by deadlines)
Document all compliance actions and communications with regulators
process_map.objective: Proactively comply with occupational H&S regulations and respond effectively to enforcement actions to avoid penalties
process_map.source_quote: Four baggage firms were fined over €1 million for persistently poor conditions; they can object to the decisions, but penalties accrue until issues are resolved.

process_map.name: Mechanisation & Improvement Programme
activities: Develop a roadmap to automate or mechanise baggage handling processes over the coming years
Allocate budget and resources to mechanisation projects (e.g., robotic loaders, improved conveyors)
Review progress on mechanisation milestones and adjust plans to meet regulatory expectations
process_map.objective: Eliminate manual heavy lifting long-term by transitioning to automated systems, in line with regulatory demands for safer working conditions
process_map.source_quote: The Inspectorate mandated that baggage handling be fully automated or mechanised in the coming years, and handlers (with Schiphol) must plan accordingly.

process_map.name: Management Oversight & Governance
activities: Hold regular management reviews of safety performance and compliance status
Assign clear accountability for H&S targets and mechanisation initiatives at executive level
Ensure sufficient resources and priority are given to safety improvements and compliance actions
process_map.objective: Maintain leadership focus and accountability on safety and compliance, ensuring continuous improvement and adherence to requirements
process_map.source_quote: The enforcement programme has been ongoing for years with multiple requirements, reflecting the need for sustained management attention to achieve compliance.

process_map.name: Stakeholder & External Coordination
activities: Collaborate with Schiphol Airport on joint safety initiatives and infrastructure (e.g., baggage system upgrades)
Engage with other baggage handling companies and airlines to share best practices and align mechanisation efforts
Consult with employee representatives/unions to address workload concerns and improve working conditions
process_map.objective: Adopt a coordinated approach with external stakeholders to ensure industry-wide improvements in physical workload and meet collective safety responsibilities
process_map.source_quote: Airlines, baggage handlers, and the airport share a collective responsibility for a safe workplace, and discussions are ongoing among all parties to lighten the workload.

native_rcr.description: Management must approve any shift schedules that risk overburdening staff (e.g., excessive overtime or consecutive heavy-lifting tasks) to ensure workload is kept at safe levels.
native_rcr.source_quote: Having employees perform more varied tasks or hiring additional staff helps reduce physical strain on workers.

native_rcr.description: Enforce mandatory task rotation for baggage handlers, alternating heavy lifting duties with lighter tasks to prevent any individual from sustaining repetitive strain over a shift.
native_rcr.source_quote: Baggage handling companies were instructed to rotate heavy lifting jobs among employees as an interim measure.

native_rcr.description: Require use of mechanical lifting aids for any baggage over a defined weight threshold, and mandate supervisors to verify that lifts and hoists are utilised for heavy items.
native_rcr.source_quote: Ensuring that lifting aids are used correctly can significantly reduce physical taxation on baggage handlers.

native_rcr.description: Perform regular maintenance checks on all lifting equipment and conveyors; any malfunctioning aid must be repaired promptly to guarantee continuous availability of mechanical assistance.
native_rcr.source_quote: Lifting aids should be available and functional at all workstations as part of the effort toward full mechanisation.

native_rcr.description: Mandate annual (and onboarding) safe-lifting and ergonomics training for all employees, with completion tracked, to reinforce awareness of proper techniques and regulatory requirements.
native_rcr.source_quote: Measures were taken to boost awareness and urgency among baggage handlers about addressing excessive physical workload.

native_rcr.description: Implement a strict incident reporting protocol: every injury or overexertion incident must be logged and investigated, with root causes identified and corrective actions implemented.
native_rcr.source_quote: Despite some improvements, the workplace still hasn’t met the required healthy standards, indicating the need to learn from each incident.

native_rcr.description: Use a safety KPI dashboard (e.g., injury frequency, average load lifted per hour, aid utilisation rate) reviewed monthly by management; define thresholds that trigger immediate review and action if exceeded.
native_rcr.source_quote: The Inspectorate will continue to check that required measures are sustained, implying the need for ongoing tracking of safety performance.

native_rcr.description: Maintain a compliance tracker for all Labour Inspectorate directives and deadlines; assign responsibility for each action item and regularly update status to ensure timely closure of obligations.
native_rcr.source_quote: A penalty (dwangsom) is incurred for each period an obligation isn’t met, underscoring the importance of meeting compliance deadlines.

native_rcr.description: Establish a formal procedure to respond to Inspectorate notices: form a task force immediately to address findings and, if needed, file an objection within the allowed timeframe.
native_rcr.source_quote: Companies have the right to file an objection against the Inspectorate’s decision, which must be exercised within a set period.

native_rcr.description: Set up a senior-level steering committee to oversee the mechanisation programme, with quarterly progress reviews to ensure the automation roadmap stays on track and meets agreed milestones.
native_rcr.source_quote: Baggage handlers, together with Schiphol, are drawing up a plan of approach to fulfil the mechanisation requirement in coming years.

completeness_gaps.description: Mechanisation roadmap not fully defined or on track (the long-term automation plan may be lacking detail, approval, or sufficient resources).
completeness_gaps.risk: Without a clear, funded mechanisation plan, the company might fail to meet the Inspectorate’s mandate for full automation, resulting in continued worker strain and future enforcement penalties.

completeness_gaps.description: Inconsistent application of interim safety measures (e.g., some teams or shifts not reliably using lifting aids or rotating tasks as required).
completeness_gaps.risk: If policies like aid usage and task rotation are not enforced uniformly, pockets of excessive physical load will persist, leading to higher injury incidence and non-compliance in those areas.

completeness_gaps.description: Insufficient monitoring tools for workload and compliance (no robust system to measure if physical load is within safe limits or if staff rotations and breaks are happening as planned).
completeness_gaps.risk: Lack of data could allow dangerous workload patterns to go unnoticed until a serious incident or external inspection occurs, undermining the company’s ability to proactively manage safety.

completeness_gaps.description: Safety culture gaps on the floor (operational pressure sometimes outweighs safety protocols; employees may skip using aids or taking breaks to meet flight schedules).
completeness_gaps.risk: A weak safety culture can negate even well-designed controls; if staff feel pressure to bypass safety measures, injury rates remain high and regulators will view the compliance as superficial.

completeness_gaps.description: Dependence on external parties for improvements (relying on Schiphol’s infrastructure changes or technology vendors for mechanisation can delay implementation of safety solutions).
completeness_gaps.risk: Delayed external support (e.g., airport-provided equipment or coordination) can slow the company’s progress towards compliance, leaving workers exposed to high physical loads and the company liable to prolonged enforcement actions outside its direct control.
